newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Appeals hearing begins for S.Korean Hanbo founder.
newsitem.headline: Appeals hearing begins for S.Korean Hanbo founder.

text.p: The Seoul High Court on Monday began hearing appeals by the founder of the troubled Hanbo Group, politicians and bankers against stiff jail sentences in a loans-for-kickbacks case, court officials said.

Last month, a Seoul criminal court jailed Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo for 15 years and nine others, including former aides to President Kim Young-sam, for between three and seven years after finding them guilty of bribery or embezzlement.
The defendants are appealing to the High Court to have their convictions dismissed or their jail terms reduced.
State prosecutors are also appealing to demand that Chung's sentence be increased to 20 years and prison terms for the rest to between eight and five years, as they had sought at the initial trial.

The scandal, involving Hanbo's failed steelmaking flagship, shattered the credibility of the president, who had led an anti-corruption drive. It also unearthed other bribery scandals that led to the arrest of President Kim's son, Kim Hyun-chul.
The lower court convicted Chung of bribing bankers and politicians to keep loans rolling in to Hanbo Steel Co, which collapsed in January under debts of five trillion won ($5.6 billion).
The steelmaker's collapse set off a chain of corporate failures and rocked the country's banking system.

Chung admitted giving tens of billions of won (tens of millions of dollars) to politicians and bankers but told the appeals court that he did not remember if he specifically asked for favours in return.
Chung, who suffered a mild stroke after his arrest in January, was carried to court by a prison officer and had to use written statements to answer questions by prosecutors and lawyers.
The other defendants are a former cabinet minister, four members of parliament, three ex-bankers and Chung's son, who is Hanbo's current chairman.
The politicians and bankers admitted taking his money, but not as bribes.
Father and son were found guilty of siphoning off a combined 364 billion won from funds belonging to the country's 14th largest business group.
